qualification.retraction: RETRACTED 2026-08-24. The 0% E1 is NOT established as a model-capability failure and this task does not currently satisfy E1. Evidence: the agent image spec2repo-agent-java:latest has NO org/javassist/javassist in its offline ~/.m2 and the agent runs with --network=none, so a candidate physically cannot resolve or compile against the javassist this spec requires. Every one of the 10 japicmp qwen trajectories inspected shows the agent discovering the gap ('javassist is not in the local repo'), hand-writing javassist stub sources under /tmp/javassist-src, compiling them into a fake javassist-3.30.2-GA.jar and installing it to ~/.m2 -- then coding self-consistently against its own stub. The symbols later reported as 'hallucinated' are the stub's own signatures: e.g. the classvalue trajectory step 42 defines 'public Annotation(String typeName)', which is exactly the constructor that failed against real javassist at scoring time. So the failure is a task-packaging / environment defect, not rule-1 model incapacity. This also makes the earlier verdict inconsistent: japicmp-specialmods-001 was REJECTED for this very reason; these 9 passed only because the stub lived in /tmp rather than in src/, so the 'no stub in src' check came back clean. STRUCTURE IS UNAFFECTED AND STILL GOOD: reference gate 100%, LINT_PASS, spec, task.json, oracle mirror. TO REQUALIFY: provision org.javassist:javassist:3.30.2-GA into the agent image's offline .m2 (as the spec declares it provided on the compile classpath), re-run qwen, and re-measure E1. Only then is a compile failure or a low pass rate attributable to the model.

e1_remeasure.note: Re-measured 2026-08-24 after two environment defects were fixed: (1) javassist 3.30.2-GA warmed into the agent image offline .m2 (docker/Dockerfile.agent.java), so a candidate can resolve and compile the dependency the spec declares instead of hand-writing a stub; (2) the oracle test classes were being discovered under the wrong name because harness/runners/java.py _CLASS_DECL matched the phrase "class sets"/"class literals" in the javadoc above the declaration, so every batch selector matched nothing and all batches came back no_report. With both fixed the candidate scores far above the E1 ceiling of 50%, so the task is rejected as too easy. The earlier 0.0 was an artefact of the environment, not difficulty.
